steps.name: QC and DESeq2 normalization of Salmon counts
steps.context: Data: /eval-four-models-v2-without-sample-scores-gsva-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (gene-level Salmon counts, 12,000 x 13 incl. gene column, Homo sapiens, colon) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-sample-scores-gsva-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 x 2). Conditions: ulcerative colitis inflamed (treated) vs control, 6v6, unpaired, single batch. Caveat from profiling: sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median. The counts file may not have length correction applied — irrelevant for DESeq2 between-sample comparison.
steps.question: Are the 12 colon samples (ulcerative colitis inflamed vs control) comparable after size-factor normalization, and what variance-stabilized expression matrix does downstream pathway scoring use — with sample_01's low library size characterized rather than silently ignored?
steps.description: Load counts.csv and metadata.csv, verify sample alignment and the 6v6 design, fit DESeq2 (design ~condition), report library sizes and per-sample gene detection with explicit attention to sample_01, and export a variance-stabilized (vst, blind=FALSE) expression matrix plus a condition-labelled PCA. Output: normalized counts CSV, vst matrix CSV, PCA PNG, QC summary.
acceptance_criteria: counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples) and metadata.csv (12 x 2) load with sample IDs matching one-to-one; 6 treated vs 6 control confirmed

library-size and per-sample gene-detection table written, explicitly flagging sample_01 (~4x below median library size) and whether its detection profile indicates a failed library or merely a smaller library
DESeq2 fit with design ~condition succeeds; size factors, normalized counts, and a vst-transformed matrix (approximately 12,000 x 12) written as CSV
PCA plot of vst values with condition labels written; a sensitivity note states whether sample_01 is an extreme outlier in PC1/PC2
vst uses blind=FALSE so the condition signal is preserved for downstream scoring

steps.name: Per-sample hallmark GSVA pathway activity scores
steps.context: Reference: the MSigDB human hallmark GMT (h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, 50 sets, HGNC symbols) is staged under /mnt/refs/managed/msigdb-hallmark-human/2026.1/. The GSVA R package (2.6.6) is installed. Input is the vst matrix and condition labels from T1S1. Salmon-derived gene identifiers may be Ensembl gene IDs rather than HGNC symbols; GSVA intersects gene sets with the matrix rows, so mismatches silently shrink sets to near-empty and must be caught by reporting coverage before trusting scores.
steps.question: What is the hallmark pathway activity score for each of the 12 samples (ulcerative colitis inflamed vs control), computed with GSVA over the 50 MSigDB hallmark sets?
steps.description: Take the vst matrix from T1S1, harmonize gene identifiers to HGNC symbols (detect Ensembl gene IDs and map via org.Hs.eg.db if needed, reporting the mapping rate), parse the staged MSigDB human hallmark GMT (50 sets), and run GSVA (kcdf='Gaussian', default min/max set size filtering) to produce a 50 x 12 pathway-activity score matrix — one score per sample per hallmark. Output: GSVA scores CSV (wide and long), gene-set coverage summary.
acceptance_criteria: Gene identifier type in counts.csv detected and reported; if Ensembl, mapped to HGNC symbols via org.Hs.eg.db with the mapping rate reported (fallback to direct use only if identifiers are already symbols)
All 50 hallmark sets parsed from the staged MSigDB human hallmark GMT; sets removed by size filtering listed with member counts, and the median set coverage in the dataset reported
GSVA run with kcdf='Gaussian' (appropriate for continuous vst values) and the version/parameters recorded in the output summary
GSVA score matrix (pathways x samples, 50 x 12 expected) written as CSV with one score per sample per hallmark — the deliverable requested in the research question
Scores exported in long format as well (sample, pathway, score, condition) for downstream plotting

steps.name: Differential hallmark activity and separation heatmap
steps.context: Input is the 50 x 12 GSVA score matrix from T1S2 plus condition labels. limma (3.68.5), ComplexHeatmap, and pheatmap are installed. With n=6 vs 6, a limma eBayes test on pathway scores is the standard readout; FDR across 50 tests is the correction basis. The heatmap is the visual deliverable of the research question, so it must show all hallmarks with the condition bar, not only significant rows.
steps.question: Which hallmark pathways separate ulcerative colitis inflamed (treated) from control samples, and what does the per-sample hallmark activity heatmap look like?
steps.description: Fit limma (design ~condition, eBayes, BH correction) on the GSVA score matrix to rank the 50 hallmarks by inflamed-vs-control difference, then draw the deliverable heatmap: z-scored hallmark scores across the 12 samples, condition annotation bar, samples grouped/ordered to expose the separation, rows ordered by effect size or clustering. Output: differential-pathway results table CSV, heatmap PNG/PDF, ranked summary of separating pathways.
acceptance_criteria: limma linear model (design ~condition) fitted on the GSVA score matrix; results table with one row per hallmark: log2FC (inflamed vs control), t, P.Value, BH-adjusted FDR, group mean scores
Group means and effect sizes reported with explicit direction (higher in inflamed vs higher in control) and an explicit statement that n=6 per group makes this exploratory

Heatmap of z-scored hallmark scores across the 12 samples written as PNG/PDF, with a condition annotation bar, samples ordered to make the treated/control separation visible, and hallmark rows ordered by clustering or effect size
Pathways that fail FDR significance still appear in the table — the heatmap shows all 50 hallmarks unless >50 are scored, so absence of significance is visible rather than hidden
A short ranked summary CSV/text names the top separating hallmarks (e.g. expected immune/inflammatory sets) with their log2FC and FDR

plan.title: UC colon hallmark GSVA scores + separation heatmap
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 12 human colon bulk RNA-seq samples (6 ulcerative colitis inflamed vs 6 control), single batch, unpaired, with raw Salmon gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 12 samples in counts.csv) and a 2-column metadata table. The deliverable is a per-sample pathway activity score matrix and a hallmark heatmap showing which pathways separate treated from control. The plan has three steps. (1) Normalize and QC: raw Salmon counts feed DESeq2 with design ~condition; size-factor normalization absorbs the library-size differences, including sample_01 which sits ~4x below the median library size — that sample is checked for collapsed gene detection (a failed library) rather than silently dropped, and a PCA of variance-stabilized values shows whether it or the condition drives sample separation. (2) Score pathways: the variance-stabilized matrix is scored with GSVA against the 50 MSigDB hallmark sets (h.all.v2026.1.Hs.symbols.gmt, confirmed staged under /mnt/refs), producing one activity score per hallmark per sample; Salmon gene identifiers may not be HGNC symbols, so identifiers are harmonized to symbols before intersecting with the gene sets (Ensembl IDs mapped via org.Hs.eg.db, with the mapping rate reported). (3) Test and visualize: limma eBayes on the GSVA score matrix ranks the 50 hallmarks by their inflamed-vs-control difference with BH FDR, and a clustered, z-scored heatmap with a condition annotation bar makes the separation visible; results are reported as exploratory given n=6 per group.
